newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA WIN FINAL WITH INSPIRED FIELDING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA WIN FINAL WITH INSPIRED FIELDING.

text.p: South Africa produced inspired out-cricket in the closing stages to pull off a dramatic victory over India in a rain-affected final of the triangular one-day series at Kingsmead on Thursday.
The South Africans, unbeaten in all seven games during the tournament, won by 17 runs after bowling India out for 234 in 39.2 overs.
Yet India, chasing an adjusted target of 251 from 40 overs after rain during the interval, appeared to be on course for victory at 198 for three in the 32nd over.

Their innings had been launched in explosive style by captain Sachin Tendulkar's imperious 45 from just 33 balls, and then sustained by fluent batting from Rahul Dravid (84) and Mohammad Azharuddin (45).
But outstanding fielding from the South Africans in the last eight overs produced two run-outs and two excellent catches to snuff out the Indian challenge.
Fast bowler Allan Donald came back from the indignity of 39 runs being taken off his first four overs to finish off the Indian tail. He ended with three for 48.
"We were up with the required run rate for most of our innings but you have to give credit to South Africa's batsmen - they batted well, as they did throughout the tournament," Tendulkar said.

"The way India came at us with the bat was a magnificent achievement and we were only too glad to win it at the death," South African captain Hansie Cronje said. "But we stuck to our guns with our fielding - and some magnificent bowling towards the end."
Earlier, South Africa put the Indian attack to the sword with a challenging 278 for eight - the highest total in the triangular competition from which Zimbabwe were eliminated.
After Cronje won his first toss of the tournament, the home side took advantage of a good batting pitch through Gary Kirsten (51), Jacques Kallis (49) and Jonty Rhodes (41).
Daryll Cullinan stroked a fluent 60 off 51 balls as the home side threatened a total in excess of 300 with six overs remaining.
But seamer Venkatesh Prasad took two wickets in consecutive deliveries in the 44th over to check South Africa's batting momentum.
